_: Bob-omb Battlefield, at Mario's own scale.
SCALE. Mario is the one character whose real height Nintendo states: 155 cm,
so he is the ruler. mario_model_mg.glb, at the scale 0.008 that every actor
placement in this level document carries, is 0.150510 level units tall in its
BIND pose — but the pose you would stand next to is su_wait, his idle, and
skinned models are measured POSED here for exactly that reason (the same rule
the XR fitting code follows: a bind pose can park limbs where the character
never puts them). Idle Mario is about 0.1415 units, a 5% slouch off the bind
pose, which gives
1.55 / 0.1415 = 10.95 metres per unit
and measured back through the viewer he stands 1.556 m. The last centimetre
is animation phase, not arithmetic; the bind pose comes out 1.65 m if you
ever want to compare against a still model.
It cross-checks twice. A Bob-omb (bombhei.glb, 13.30 model units) comes out
1.16 m — chest height on Mario, which is what it looks like in game. And the
course measures 175 x 50 x 175 m, so the mountain is a sixteen-storey climb.
Both are the right kind of number.
SPAWN. Not chosen: the game's own. Level object type 1 is an entrance record
and the level's FIRST one is where the player spawns (writeup Part V section
2, handler $020FE6C8); cmd/exportlevelobjs already emits it, and for this
level it reads [-6.225, 1.7, 6.353] with yaw 135.
The 1.7 is deliberately not used. That is the height Mario is dropped from —
you fall into a course in SM64 — while this preset wants the floor, which
both the collision mesh and the visible mesh put at y = 0 under that exact
x/z.
FACING. rotY is degrees (webexport main.go:994 multiplies by pi/180), and 135
under dir = (sin, 0, cos) is (0.707, 0, -0.707): from the corner the entrance
sits in, toward the middle of the course and up the rising ground. The other
convention would face you off the edge of the map.
_sky: vr01.glb is 59,000 units across — a 645 km dome at this scale, which is to
say outside any far plane worth having and therefore not drawn at all.
scale:auto brings it inside the frustum and forces painter's order, because
a dome pulled in to a few hundred metres would otherwise be depth-tested
against a 175 m course and sliced open by its own hills.
The radius is not what makes it read as sky: the viewer centres the dome on
the EYE being drawn rather than on the head, so both eyes get the identical
image and the binocular disparity is exactly zero. Head-centred at this same
radius, the nearest part of this dome subtends 338 arcseconds — an order of
magnitude above the 20-30 arcsecond stereoacuity threshold, which is why it
still read as close after merely being scaled up.
_fog: Daylight, so this is aerial perspective and not a torch: distance haze only,
no flicker. The colour is sampled from the game's own sky — the lightest band
of vr01's 256x256 gradient, which is its horizon.
_floor: The game's own walkable surface (the level's .kcl, exported as the hidden
col_bombhei_map layer) rather than the art. Checked against the visible mesh
over a 0.25-unit lattice: 3,955 sample points have floor under both, 132
under the art only, none under collision only, and 98.7% of the shared points
agree on height to within half a metre. maxSlope 50 because Mario's hills are
_props: Mario, two metres ahead and facing the way you are, because he is the ruler
this whole preset is measured with — if he does not come up to your eyes,
metresPerUnit is wrong. scale 0.008 is the same factor every actor placement
in the level document carries; su_wait is his idle clip, which the object
document lists and the model's shared data/player skeleton animates.
